segments.title: Chương 185: 0185 【Lý Ngạo Chân Nhận Chức】
segments.content:
Chapter 188 0185 Li Ao Actually Signed Up

Li Ao had once said he didn't use computers because the information online was too jumbled and hard to discern.

But that raised a question: if he didn't use a computer, how did he know the information online was too jumbled?

This indicated that not only had he used a computer, but he had also been online!

It was just that he found it frustrating to use, so he abandoned it.

"Throw them out, they're all useless," Li Ao said as he ran off to take a shower.

His wife, Wang Xiaotun, inspected them carefully again, tossing them into the trash can one by one. When she got to the slip of paper, she unfolded it and saw that besides the web address, there was another line of text: If Mr. Li registers an account and needs identity verification, please call this number...

She didn't throw it away, but slipped it into her own pocket.

Wang Xiaotun turned on the computer and browsed mainland portal websites, specifically looking for news about her husband. In this era, the firewalls on both sides weren't too severe, and non-sensitive websites were accessible.

The news about Li Ao was basically all positive.

But in the comment sections below the news, the tone was starkly different. Good grief, people were saying all sorts of things.

Some were even cursing Chen Guiliang.

Others were explaining things for Chen Guiliang, and they included a link to his latest blog post.

Li Ao had already finished his shower and returned, but Wang Xiaotun was still reading the news comments.

"What are you looking at?" Li Ao asked.

Wang Xiaotun said, "A lot of mainland netizens are cursing you."

Li Ao chuckled, "Let them."

Wang Xiaotun added, "The Beida student who gave you the note is also being cursed at. I'm reading the article he wrote to explain."

Li Ao pulled a chair over and sat with his wife to read.

《Regarding the Controversy of Li Ao's Beida Speech and an Explanation of My Own Words and Actions》

"It seems I've been getting cursed at recently. Since some people can't seem to understand what I'm saying, I'll now explain it to you in detail..."

"Mr. Li Ao was definitely a bit unhappy about this trip to Beida. First, when Lien Chan came to speak, Beida rolled out a red carpet, but they didn't for him this time. Second, Lien Chan's speech was broadcast in its entirety, while his had to be selectively broadcast."

"Why did this happen? Because Lien Chan is a political figure, so he got the red carpet treatment. Moreover, political figures are measured in their speech, so a full broadcast is certainly not a problem..."

"It was precisely because of Li Ao's displeasure that he started by poking fun at Lien Chan right from the beginning. Midway through, I think he wanted to hold it in, but he really couldn't. Those 30 minutes of rambling and letting himself loose had a strong sense of emotional venting. But he still hadn't vented completely, so he used a joking tone to curse Beida on the spot for being too spineless..."

"The first point you're all cursing me for is that Li Ao said Beida was too spineless, and as a Beida student, I didn't refute it and even said I basically agreed with his view..."

"Come on, everyone. When a guest can't help but throw a tantrum, can the host curse back? There were hundreds of Beida teachers and students there, and they were all laughing and applauding at the time. Let me state that I didn't applaud then. It's not because I was unhappy, but because I disagreed with him using Cai Yuanpei as an example to prove that the current Beida is too spineless..."

"During the Q&A, why did I deliberately say his part about the Beiyang warlords was incorrect? And deliberately point out the close friendship between the Minister of Education and the President of Beida at the time? It was to subtly refute that his later example was problematic! Did you think I was only objecting to the part about the Beiyang warlords?"

"He said the Beiyang Ministry of Education gave an order, and the President of Beida ignored it. The Beiyang Ministry of Education sent money, and the President of Beida accepted it. He used this to prove Beida's moral integrity at the time. And used this to prove that the current Beida is too spineless, not even daring to broadcast his speech in full..."

"Minister of Education Mr. Fan and Beida President Mr. Cai, since these two were close friends, there are two possibilities: First, when Mr. Fan was in his position, nothing Mr. Cai did was dangerous. Second, after Mr. Fan resigned, everything Mr. Cai did was wrong. Whether Beida was obedient at the time or not, the outcome would have been the same."

"So I was subtly pointing out that Mr. Li Ao's use of this example fails to prove that Beida was impressive back then. Likewise, it cannot lead to the conclusion that the current Beida is too spineless. I gave him face, my refutation was veiled. Did you all really not see it?"

Reading this, Li Ao lit a cigarette and exhaled a cloud of smoke without a word.

Wang Xiaotun asked, "Did you catch his hidden meaning back then?"

"No," Li Ao shook his head.

Because when he had cursed Beida for being spineless, it was purely an emotional outburst. Once he had vented, it was over. He didn't think about the consequences at all and didn't care about the matter in the slightest.

He hadn't expected that while Chen Guiliang was refuting his comments on the Beiyang warlords, he was also refuting his later criticism of Beida.

Li Ao suddenly muttered, "He said back then that for some people, speaking is no better than farting. Could he have been subtly referring to me?"

Wang Xiaotun smiled without saying anything.

The article wasn't finished.

"During Mr. Li Ao's speech, there were 30 minutes of him letting loose, rambling on about many things. Some of the content, like the part about the Beiyang warlords, was pure nonsense..."

"Let's take his comments on Marx as an example. Mr. Li Ao may not have truly studied him, or perhaps his study was not deep enough. Marx told Engels that he himself was not a Marxist. Mr. Li Ao cited this to conclude that 'Marx himself didn't believe in Marxism.'"

"But what is the reality?"

"In 19th-century Germany and France, some self-proclaimed Marxists did not truly understand or practice Marxism, and were even doing things that went against it. Marx wanted to draw a clear line between himself and those self-proclaimed Marxists! And he was also firmly opposing dogmatism!"

"Engels made a statement on this: Marxism is not a dogma, but a method. It provides no ready-made dogmas, but rather a starting point for further investigation and the method for that investigation."

"No one is an absolute authority. We shouldn't believe every word the masters say. Much of what Mr. Li Ao says in his speeches can just be taken as jokes."

"When I said I basically agreed with his views, I was agreeing with his views on major issues of right and wrong. For example, I agreed even more with the views he expressed in his later speech at Tsinghua."

"As long as we agree on the major issues of right and wrong, I believe we can be considered to be on the same path. Conflicts over minor points of view can be completely ignored; we can seek common ground while reserving differences."

Li Ao's face burned a little after reading.

He really hadn't known the historical context of Marx's statement. He had used it as a novel point to make jokes on more than one occasion.

Now, seeing Chen Guiliang lay the facts bare, it was as if Chen Guiliang had slapped him in the face in public.

He had said this several times before, which meant he had been slapped in the face several times.

In the past, when Li Ao argued with people, he could always gain the upper hand because his opponents' words were full of loopholes. But now, Chen Guiliang was purely stating facts and reasoning, and Li Ao simply couldn't refute him.

This was true for the Beiyang warlords segment, and it was true for the Marx segment as well.

That night, Li Ao tossed and turned, unable to sleep, wanting to say something to save face.

Because he had seen the comments under Chen Guiliang's article.

Some of them were as follows:

"I read the text live-stream of the speech and wanted to refute this part right then. Haha, I'm a graduate student at the School of Marxism. Actually, you don't need a master's degree, any undergraduate in a related field should know this."

"Sigh, the part where Li Ao used Bo Yi and Shu Qi as an example was also a complete mismatch between argument and evidence. I thought about it for a long time and still couldn't figure out the logical connection. There's just no fucking logic!"

"To be honest, I'm a little disappointed in Li Ao."

How to describe a person like Li Ao?

Sometimes he would never admit his mistakes, and other times he would generously admit them.

Whether he admitted it or not depended on his own thoughts and mood at the time.

The next day, he wrote an article and handed it to his wife, saying, "Help me register an account and post this article online."

Whether he used a computer or went online also depended purely on his own ideas.

The him who, in another time and space, claimed not to use a computer, had become a Weibo user very early on. Since he couldn't operate it or type, he had his wife do it for him, and later switched to using a touchscreen with handwriting.

Moreover, his frequency of posting on Weibo was exceptionally high...
